title: Room Type
description: A style-independent room. Rooms sit between the element slot and the massing: a massing is the skeleton, a room is an organ, and a grouping is a system. Like massings, rooms are NOT style — a parlor and a living room may be the same volume in the same position doing different social work, and the same room wears different trim in every style that contains it. What a room actually constrains is dimension, daylight, adjacency and servicing, and those are physical facts before they are stylistic ones.

aka.description: The same room under other names and other centuries — parlour, sitting room, living room, front room, great room. Naming is where most of the confusion in residential design lives.

function_class.description: What the room is FOR, independent of what it is called.

description.description: What it is, what it was for, and what it feels like to be in one.

note.description: Rooms are social institutions before they are spaces. The parlor did not shrink because houses got smaller; it died because the funeral moved out of the house.

proportion.description: Length:width ratio band. Vernacular rooms cluster near 1.25; Palladio's seven shapes give the formal set.

critical_dimension.description: The one measurement that decides whether the room works, and why. Usually set by furniture or by a single act — the length of a laid table, the swing of a door, the reach from a hearth.

furniture.description: What has to fit, with clearances. This is the real constraint on a room and it is almost never written down, which is why so many plans have rooms that dimension correctly and cannot be furnished.

clearance_in.description: The gap this item needs beyond its own footprint, in inches. It must be STATED: a zero is a real answer and says the item needs no gap -- because it is itself clear space (a passing route, an arrival floor, a landing) or because it has no floor bulk (a mirror, a bell pull). Null was permitted here until 26 Aug 2026 and meant nothing distinguishable: build/plan_check.py read it as zero, so an item whose clearance an author simply forgot was checked as though it needed none. The twenty records that carried null all genuinely meant zero and now say so (OQ 52).

needs_uninterrupted_wall_ft.description: WP-7.2. A run of wall this item needs UNBROKEN BY OPENINGS, in feet. Authored only where the room's own `note` states it in words, and the note is the basis — the number sits beside the sentence so the two cannot drift. One item carries it today: the dining room's sideboard, whose note reads 'Needs an uninterrupted wall of at least 6 ft. This is what the second window usually kills.' `plan_check`'s drawn layer measures the longest run each wall has left once the placement's doors and windows have taken theirs. This is an ARRANGEMENT rule and never a sizing one: room size comes from the program and the catalogue band, never from the furniture (OQ 79, ruled 27 Aug 2026).

placement.description: Freestanding items need clearance on both sides of the short dimension; anything against a wall needs it on one. Getting this wrong makes every galley kitchen and butler's pantry fail its own furniture check.

depth_multiplier.description: Maximum useful room depth as a multiple of window head height. Roughly 2.25 for a primary living room, less behind a porch.

sides_lit.description: How many walls should carry glass for the room to work.

orientation.description: Preferred aspect and why — a kitchen wants morning, a parlor wants afternoon, a dairy wants north.

depth_governs.description: Whether the depth-against-window-head rule applies to this room at all. Defaults to true. False marks a room the rule was never written for -- a garage is deeper than any window can light and is not thereby defective. This is JUDGED-WHERE-THE-JUDGMENT-DOES-NOT-APPLY, which is a different claim from 'unjudged' (could not evaluate) and from 'passed' (evaluated and clear); a checker must not collapse it into either. Ruled as OQ 31.

adjacency.description: The join point to the plan-logic slot group, and the reason this catalogue exists. Rules are directional and typed.

entered_from.description: room ids or circulation types this room may legitimately be entered from

privacy_rank.description: 0 street, 1 threshold, 2 public, 3 family, 4 private, 5 intimate. The gradient a plan must not scramble: a bedroom off a formal hall is a rank-4 room opening onto a rank-2 space.

stack_proximity_ft.description: How close this room must be to a waste stack. The single most common cause of a plan that cannot be built as drawn.

style_variation.description: How the room differs by style — name, size, position, trim grade, and whether it exists at all. This is the style facet; the room itself stays neutral.

conflict.description: Where the code minimum and good practice diverge — the code is a floor and is routinely mistaken for a target.

massing_fit.description: massing ids this room sits in comfortably

slots.description: element slots that matter most in this room

void.description: Only meaningful on a room whose `function_class` is `outdoor`. OQ 55, ruled 24 Aug 2026: the placement engines carry outdoor rooms as reserved voids -- placed and dimensioned, excluded from the area budget and from the heated envelope, drawn open. To place one you have to know two facts about it that no field carried, and they are independent: whether the void sits INSIDE the block outline (a courtyard, a Charleston piazza) or is appended to it at grade (a terrace), and whether it is ROOFED (a loggia is; a courtyard is not). The first decides whether it takes a rectangle in the footprint; the second decides whether anything may sit above it. Absent, a room is treated as `within_footprint: false` -- the behaviour before this ruling, which is to leave it out of placement entirely. This is not the `void` function_class the ruling rejected as option (b): function_class is untouched, nothing is re-typed, and the field is descriptive rather than a second classification axis.

within_footprint.description: True when the void occupies a rectangle inside the building's own block -- the house is built around it or beside it under one outline. False when it is appended at grade and the block would be the same shape without it.

roofed.description: True when the void is covered -- under the main roof or a shed off it. An unroofed void is a hole in the roof plane and nothing may be placed over it; a roofed one will carry an upper storey (a Charleston single's upper piazza sits on its lower one).

relation.description: How the two rooms are related. `open-to-below` and `open-to-above` are VERTICAL and were added by OQ 57: a room may be open to a double-height volume on the storey beneath it, which is the whole of what an overlook is, and no arrangement within one level can satisfy that. plan_check.py evaluates them across levels.

exceptions.description: styles or types where the rule does not hold

via.description: Room types that legitimately stand between. A direct-door rule with no `via` forbids the very room invented to satisfy it — the butler's pantry between kitchen and dining is the standing case.

vertical_ok.description: Whether a normally horizontal rule is ALSO satisfied by the target sitting directly above or below. Added by OQ 57 for the case the corpus could not express: a great chamber over the parlour is a drawing room, and drawing-room's hard rule that it must reach a dining room is a GROUND-FLOOR rule -- an upper-floor state room can satisfy it only vertically, and without this it trips a fatal for the one arrangement the type is famous for. Defaults to false, so no existing rule changes meaning.
